4. Repeated repair at constant wall gauge has a material destination, not only a heating time.

Using the declared film dimensions in the P2 available design as an INTRODUCED geometry:20 patches of80mm2 at.038mm supply60.8mm3;98% transfer gives59.584mm3. Debiting4.655mm3 old material leaves54.929mm3 net additional solid. At the original gauge this corresponds to1445.5mm2 of single-layer area. Restoring the original local gauge therefore requires an actual larger receiving area, flow into another stock, cutting/capture, or other mass-removal operation. Heating cannot erase material. This is not evidence that an actual patch fails.

Six extra local patches minus one.931mm3 removal leave17.309mm3, corresponding to455.5mm2 at.038mm, compared with an80mm2 patch footprint. Eight nominal equal layers are.304mm thick. For equal linear elastic thin plates the fully bonded bending rigidity scales as n^3 and freely sliding layers as n, giving512 versus8 relative to one layer. The simple outer-fibre strain at2mm radius is7.6%. Actual TPU is large-strain, viscoelastic and temperature/history dependent; these are scaling diagnostics, not a measured modulus, fatigue law, weld toughness, failure prediction or installed-guide result.

An alternative constant-gauge scarf/butt insertion would require removing and capturing old material, forming controlled edges, holding a thin curved opening, restoring load transfer and independently releasing its tools. A rolling material transport could instead move a repaired region out of a flexing zone, but its extra wall inventory, changed working geometry and finite unused region are paid stocks. Neither alternative has been constructed here. The thin-film replacement comparator is genuinely strong; a few grams of prepared stock cannot be treated as a massive complete actuator.
